missionPremise: OPS-24 law 3: Burnet is the first county through the farm, and the farm's machinery is built and refined during that run. The farm had a row for its manifest (P-187), its merge gate (P-198) and its per-stage checks (P-197) and NOTHING TO WALK THE THIRTEEN STAGES WITH. P-284 (stage and cost records) and P-281 (heavy-scan leases) are live as of 2026-09-17, which is what this row waited on: a runner can now record each stage as it goes and leave the heavy windows to the jobs that already take them. The dispatch's own frame is a SKELETON that is honest about what it cannot do yet, because the thirteen stages are not all built -- so the first thing this lane measured was which of them have a runner TODAY, and the answer (5 of 13 stages, 8 of 15 steps not built) is printed by every dry run rather than implied.
completionPredicate: A stranger can evaluate this from a fresh clone of this branch after `npm install`, with no store and no credential: (1) `node --test test/p285-county-runner.test.mjs` -> 27 tests, 27 pass, 0 fail, covering all four pre-registered falsifiers, the resume grain, the stop-point flags and the plan's consistency; (2) `node --test test/p285-county-runner-live.test.mjs` with FACTORY_DATABASE_URL aimed at a scratch PostgreSQL carrying the factory migrations -> 3 tests, 3 pass, 0 fail, including the live dry run for 48053 whose 15 rows are audited field by field; (3) `node --test --test-concurrency=1 test/*.test.mjs` on this branch -> 1594 tests / 1589 pass / 1 fail, and a pristine worktree of 47c7dfc on the same store -> 1564 / 1559 / 1, with the SAME failing set (test/ctx-b3-store-census.test.mjs:137, which needs a pinned LDT checkout, and two test/p3-absence.test.mjs non-vacuity findings whose own names say they are out of scope), so the delta is exactly this lane's 30 new tests; (4) `node src/cli.mjs county-runner --county=48053 --manifest=<file>` prints thirteen stages in order with each step's job or its NOT BUILT code, its instrument, its resume token, its lease and its stop points, executes nothing, and writes fifteen run_mode='dry-run' stage records and no runs row. The ROW ITSELF IS NOT CUSTOMER-DONE and cannot be graded here: the dispatch forbids running any stage job or the runner with --apply, so the skeleton's own grade is Burnet's run records after the integration seat runs it.

falsifier: All four pre-registered falsifiers PASSED, with two wording amendments and ONE design correction that the test suite itself produced. The amendments are declared, not buried: F1's refusal code is two codes in the implementation (NOT_NAMED for a defaulted path, UNREADABLE for a named one), and F4's 'thirteen records' is fifteen because the declared step grain gives stage 6 and stage 10 two steps each. Recorded so a reader comparing the dispatch's one-flag sentence with the implementation finds the reason, not a discrepancy.

LESSON: A claim about ANOTHER FILE is worth a test that reads that file. This lane's plan asserted 'the stage 6 jobs take the P-281 lease themselves'. The claim was half right: two of eleven jobs do, and the publish holds a window nobody had written down. A one-screen test that reads src/jobs/<verb>.mjs for grantHeavyScanLease( and compares it with the plan's own declarations failed on the first run, in the direction nobody expects (a step claiming a lease its jobs do not take) and listed the job that had been missed. Prose in a plan drifts; a test that reads the file the prose is about does not.

A connection is a resource with an owner, and a runner that does not say who owns it will hang rather than fail. connectFactory returns a pg.Client; a Client keeps the event loop alive; the first live run printed its plan, wrote its 15 records and then hung forever. The fix is three lines (client.end() in a finally, conditional on who connected) but the DETECTION is what matters: report the fact on the result (connectionClosedByRunner) so a caller and a test can see it, because 'the process did not exit' is invisible in a CI log.

A resume point that an operator cannot type is not a resume point. The first draft's --from took a stage number, which silently re-ran stage 10's staging step to reach production -- the exact 'completed stage runs again' failure the dispatch forbids. Making the token name a STEP (10:production) costs one function and makes the printed instruction copy-pasteable.

Recording a dry run per STEP needs a denominator stated out loud. 'Thirteen rows' reads as 'thirteen runners'; the tally ('5/13 stages have a runner; 8 steps are not built') printed next to the plan is what stops a reader counting thirteen rows as a green program.

Two live test files that share a scratch store are coupled even when neither names the other. This lane's 15 Burnet rows broke P-284's store-wide view assertion twice: once as leftover state and once -- the one that matters -- because node runs test files in parallel. If a test asserts something about a WHOLE store, it is asserting it about every future writer's data too; the same class of fragility was P-292's Bastrop fixture, in a different costume.
